digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store doctor / push reconciliation
propositions: When two git bundles exist for a single S3 ref, git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects the operation before writing anything, and git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads causing fresh clones to fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable

Upstream's interactive Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is unusable for autonomous fleets (blocks on input() at EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's events via orphan branching or deletion, causing irreversible data loss in an append-only event log store

Rebar's existing sync._do_reconverge/_union_merge already implements lossless divergent-head reconciliation via iterated 2-parent git merge with --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated histories, following the consensus pattern across restic/git-annex/jj/Fossil

A non-interactive S3 doctor must detect the multi-bundle signature ('multiple bundles exists on server' or 'multiple updates for ref'), acquire the helper's per-ref lock, fetch all divergent bundle heads, merge them losslessly under rebar's write_lock following sync's semantics, write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any original, and release the lock

The heal must write the merged bundle before deleting originals and never delete the merged tip itself, so a crash at any point leaves at least one bundle carrying the full merged history, enabling recovery by re-running the heal idempotently

Detection in push_tickets_branch's retry loop must invoke heal_multi_bundle exactly once (guarded by healed_once flag) before normal non-FF recovery to prevent infinite retry loops, and concurrent repairs are serialized via the helper's own acquire_lock/release_lock mechanism so only one process merges while others back off
